p.s: Using UGC in ads, store and social channels

p.t:
Real customer photos and videos often beat polished ads.
Use real customer material in retargeting, which means ads shown again to people who already saw the product.

Only boost new accounts. Boosting old, successful posts can kill their free sales.
Borrowed clips from others risk copyright strikes, so use them only for a short time.
Paid ads: why UGC works
p.s: Using UGC in ads, store and social channels

p.t: **UGC** (user-generated content, meaning real customer material such as reviews and photos of people using the product) builds trust.
It works especially well in retargeting ads, where it answers the doubts of people who already saw the product.
Meta (the company behind Facebook and Instagram) favors content that looks natural.
Over-produced ads still run but cost more, so **real customer photos and videos**, or phone-shot footage, often perform better.
Use **real customer videos or photos** in retargeting where possible. A customer describing their experience often outperforms a brand message.
**Spark Ads** (a real post from a creator's account, run as an ad) from influencers (people with large followings who promote products) tend to outperform regular brand ads.
They look like organic content (free, unpaid posts) from a trusted creator, not like a sales message. This lowers viewer resistance (how much people push back) and makes the ad feel more credible.
Turn collected UGC into paid ads.
p.h: Paid ads: where the traffic goes

p.t: Cold audiences (people who have never seen the brand) rarely buy on direct product pages.
So **send paid traffic** (paid visitors) to the influencer's profile or to a lead magnet page (a free offer that collects an email address) instead of the product page.

A creative is the ad itself, such as a video or an image.
**Cold**
Creative: UGC video ads with real creators

Send traffic to: Influencer's profile or lead magnet page
**Retargeting (people who already saw the product)**
Creative: Real customer videos or photos
Send traffic to: Not specified in the source

p.h: Paid ads: whitelisting and brand pages

p.t: content for brands). These creators come from TikTok Shop creator programs (TikTok's own program linking brands with creators) or official Instagram influencers.
**Whitelisting** (running ads through a creator's or persona page, an account built around a character, instead of the brand's own page) means exactly that.
The brand's page can still host the UGC content, so **both approaches** are used together.
Paid ads: boosting organic content
p.s: Using UGC in ads, store and social channels

p.t: **Boosting** (paying to push a post) with Coins (TikTok's paid boost currency) or Spark Ads on a brand-new account can
speed up reaching the right audience. This works during the new account advantage window (extra early reach for new accounts), which lasts roughly the first **one to two weeks**.
Use this boost only on new accounts.
**Do not boost old accounts** with established organic performance (proven free reach). Boosting old successful organic posts has been reported to kill organic sales.
Use organic videos as ad creatives only if they already reached **around 50,000 to 100,000 views** and carry real social proof (signs that other people trust it, such as comments and likes).
Very new organic videos can lose organic reach when boosted through Spark Ads.
**Both conditions apply together:** the view threshold decides which videos qualify, and the account-age rule decides whether boosting is safe at all.

Replace the borrowed clips with your own UGC once the product gains traction (starts selling well).
Ads with low attention (few people watch or stop to look) can be improved rather than discarded.
Layer a UGC video with a voice-over (spoken narration added over footage) or new hooks (the first seconds that grab attention). A **single hook change** can lift attention and sales.

p.h: Converting winning UGC into other formats

p.t: to buy) and better traction (a growing response) than static image ads (still pictures) in the tests. Static image ads still work, but **UGC AI ads** are the better default for this product type.
Convert a proven UGC AI ad concept (an idea that already worked) back to image ads, in this order:
1. Confirm the UGC AI concept has produced **many purchases** and steady profit.
2. Build image ads that use the same concept, angle (the point of view of the ad) and pain point (the problem the customer has).
3. Run the image ads alongside the UGC AI ads and **compare** soft metrics (views and clicks) and hard metrics (sales and profit).
Product pages and testimonial sections
p.s: Using UGC in ads, store and social channels

p.t: Place **customer photos** in a dedicated section (its own separate block) on the product page,
not mixed into supplier product photos. This section is one of the most important elements for conversion (turning visitors into buyers).
Customer photos also work in blog posts where a product image fits.
A standalone customer photo gallery page (a page with only customer photos) is **a weaker use** of the photos than product pages and emails.
In testimonial sections (blocks of customer quotes) and product images, use **raw UGC photos** of real customers in real-life settings instead of high-quality studio shots.
Visitors relate more to real people, and reported results show that such content converts better than polished lifestyle images.
Pattern (a repeatable layout): **place review screenshots** (pictures of reviews) from the store, a marketplace (a shared shopping site that sells many
sellers' products) or a product page over a blurred version of the product. Show the store URL (web address) in the same frame.
It works because it puts several genuine reviews in one image while the product stays visible in the background.
Example 1: **Five** screenshots of five-star reviews with the URL of the store at the bottom.
Example 2: **Three** reviews from a marketplace over a blurred kitchen counter with the product.
Formula (a fill-in pattern): **name a real customer** with their location, state that they like the product,
and mention one specific benefit (one concrete advantage). Messenger is Facebook's chat app. Real names and places increase trust more than generic praise.
Example 1: Maria from Ohio told us this kettle heats up in **under three minutes**, and she uses it every morning.
Example 2: Dan from Texas wrote that his backpack survived **a full semester** of daily use.
Video bubbles on the website
p.s: Using UGC in ads, store and social channels

p.t: Video bubbles are small round video previews.
Embed (place code so the content appears on your site) a bubble group (a set of bubbles shown together) on the website, as follows:
1. **Create** the video campaigns (groups of ads with one goal) that will be shown as bubbles.

2. **Group** the campaigns together into one bubble group (playlist, a set of videos shown together) per topic.
3. **Embed** the bubble group on the website.
4. **Customize** the bubbles to match the look and feel (colors and style) of the website.
5. **Update** the content later without re-embedding, because embedded bubbles are fully dynamic (they change when you update them).
6. **Reuse** any video that is already embedded in email marketing campaigns.
Shoppable means customers can buy straight from the picture.
Add a carousel (a row you swipe through) of social content (posts from social media) to the website, as follows:

1. **Pull** the content directly from your Instagram or TikTok account onto the website.
2. **Tag** each video with the specific products shown in it.

3. **Place** the carousel on the home page, collection pages (pages that group products) or product pages. There it works like an endless scroll (a never-ending feed) for product discovery (finding products).
4. **Let** the customer check out from the carousel with a single click.
Scaling means growing sales.
p.h: Scaling case: UGC as the main lever

p.t: Starting point: a brand scaled mainly on bottom-of-funnel static ads (ads aimed at people ready to buy, using still pictures) for about **two years**, with three UGC videos.
Change: UGC video was introduced **a couple of months earlier**.
Result: monthly revenue (money coming in each month) rose about **5x** with both formats combined.
Conclusion: **UGC is the main scaling lever** (the thing that grows sales most), while bottom-of-funnel statics help at small scale or on top of existing UGC.
